notes: RECONSTRUCTED (not contemporary) key: Satoshi Tomokiyo's reconstruction of the Villeparisis cipher (1564), BnF fr.16039, published on cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/henryiii.htm ('Villeparisis, Resident in Rome (1564)' section): 'BnF fr.16039 (Gallica) contains cipher letters from Rome to Charles IX and Queen Mother, Catherine de Medici. A letter (1564) (f.17) of Henri Cleutin, Seigneur de Villeparisis ... used the following cipher.' Row 1 = primary glyph per plaintext letter (headers a b c d e f g h i l m n o p q r s t u x y z). Homophone rows exist (row 2: zeta/i, 8/o, sp/r, omega/s, etc.) but were NOT systematically transcribed - column alignment too uncertain at this resolution; only row 1 used. The z-column row-1 glyph was off-crop; left unmapped. Word tables below the pink bars ('con dit? de(s) du ...', 'par parler pour que ...') were NOT transcribed. NOTE: this is a DIFFERENT key from the Colbert 390 Rennes key (compare: Villeparisis cipher 'd'->plain 'h' vs Rennes cipher 'd'->plain 'e'; Villeparisis 'p'->'s' vs Rennes 'p'->'b').
source: Satoshi Tomokiyo, cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/henryiii.htm, 'Villeparisis, Resident in Rome (1564)'.
